formula: wish + past simple (present wish) · wish + had + participle (past regret) · wish + would (annoyance) · wish + could (ability) · if only (emphatic)
formula_visual: [I wish I knew] (now) // [I wish I'd known] (then) // [I wish he'd stop] (annoyance)
when_to_use: 'wish + past simple' for a present situation you want to be different. 'wish + past perfect' for regret about the past. 'wish + would' to complain about someone else's repeated behaviour. 'if only' is the emphatic version of all three. Use 'were' for all persons after wish.
when_to_use_ar: 'wish + ماضٍ بسيط' لوضع حاضر تريده مختلفًا. 'wish + ماضٍ تام' للأسف على الماضي. 'wish + would' للشكوى من سلوك متكرر. 'if only' الصيغة التوكيدية.
why_arabic_speakers_struggle: Arabic يا ليت covers all of these with one structure, so learners don't shift the tense back. They also say 'I wish I would have known' by blending the wish and third-conditional patterns, and use 'wish + will' for the future.

examples.en: I wish I knew the answer.
I wish I'd studied harder at school.
examples.ar: أتمنى لو درست بجد في المدرسة (أسف)

examples.en: I wish he'd stop making that noise.
examples.ar: أتمنى لو يتوقف عن ذلك الضجيج (تضايق)

examples.en: If only I'd listened to you!

common_errors.wrong: I wish I would have known.
common_errors.explanation: Past regret after 'wish' uses the past perfect, not 'would have'.

common_errors.wrong: I wish I will pass the exam.
common_errors.correct: I hope I'll pass the exam.
common_errors.explanation: 'wish' is not used for realistic future hopes — use 'hope'.
After 'wish' the modal shifts back: can → could.

practice_fill_blank.sentence: I wish I ___ (study) harder at school.
I wish he ___ (stop) making that noise.

quick_rule: Present wish → wish + past. Past regret → wish + had + participle. Annoyance → wish + would. Realistic future → use 'hope', not 'wish'.
quick_rule_ar: أمنية حاضرة → wish + ماضٍ. أسف ماضٍ → wish + had + التصريف. تضايق → wish + would. مستقبل واقعي → استخدم hope.
mnemonic: Step the tense back one level. 'hope' for the real future, 'wish' for the unreal.
connect_to_speaking: In accent week 7 you drilled /aɪwɪʃaɪd/ and regret prosody. Say 'I wish I'd STUDied harder ↘' with a breath first and a falling tone — the grammar alone won't sound like regret.
